review_notes:
I reviewed all 199 lines. I read the definitions of `referenceFamily`, `referenceLabels`/`referenceOriginalLabel` and `referenceFamily_physicalPacket` (SourceReferenceRestriction.lean), and `sum_reference_frozen` (SourceReferenceMainRestriction.lean). I also read `constant` (SourceSlottedLattice.lean), `absoluteConstant` and `snappedSite` (SourceLabeledRawEnvelope.lean), `positiveEnvelope` (SourceLabeledSynthesisEnvelope.lean), `snappedLatticeSite` (SnappedLattice.lean), `physicalFrozenCenteredCoefficient` (SourceLabeledCoefficientSplit.lean) and `analyzingCoefficient`. I checked the downstream uses in SourceLabeledNarrowTail.lean, SourceAssignedPathIntegral.lean and SourceAssignedStoppedBound.lean.

The file restricts everything to the equal-slope reference family `referenceFamily t t`. For the snapped-site and positive-envelope lemmas this is necessary: with different slopes, `snappedLatticeSite` changes because both originZ and rowSlope shift by (old-new). For the coefficient, main-scale and masked-band identities it is also necessary: with different slopes the coefficient would evaluate `b` and `|v z - t|` at the new slope, so generalising would need a re-parametrisation of `b` and `v`, which is beyond a simple generalisation. The exception is the constant lemmas, which ignore the slopes entirely; that is the one finding.

I considered a per-component version of `physicalFrozenCenteredCoefficient_eq_zero` that assumes `b j l k t = 0` for a single `k`. I did not report it, because every caller (`sum_reference_frozen`'s `hvanish`) needs the hypothesis for all `k` anyway. I have not compiled the proposed general lemma, but an existing proof with distinct slopes (`assignedInhabitedReference_constant`) uses the same unfold-then-`ring` approach.

findings.excerpt:
theorem referenceSelf_constant :
    (Q).constant = P.absoluteConstant*(F*cone+2) := by
  unfold constant absoluteConstant referenceFamily
  ring
findings.problem: Through the notation `Q` = `P.referenceFamily t t R cone w F ...`, both lemmas are stated only for the equal-slope reference family. But `constant` reads only `carrierBound`, `profileBound`, `order` and `ratioBound`. `referenceFamily` sets `carrierBound := F*cone` and copies the other three from `P`, independent of `oldSlope` and `newSlope`. The specialisation to `t t` is therefore unnecessary. As a result, families built with distinct slopes (e.g. `assignedReferenceFamily`, which uses `referenceFamily oldSlope (T top).slope`) cannot reuse these lemmas and re-derive the identity by unfolding.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a general version (and optionally keep the self-version as a specialisation so existing call sites are unchanged):

theorem referenceFamily_constant (oldSlope newSlope : ℝ) :
    (P.referenceFamily oldSlope newSlope R cone w F hw hcone hF hwide hfrequency).constant =
      P.absoluteConstant*(F*cone+2) := by
  unfold constant absoluteConstant referenceFamily
  ring

theorem referenceFamily_absoluteConstant (oldSlope newSlope : ℝ) :
    (P.referenceFamily oldSlope newSlope R cone w F hw hcone hF hwide hfrequency).absoluteConstant =
      P.absoluteConstant := rfl

The proofs are unchanged: unfolding `referenceFamily` exposes `carrierBound := F*cone` and P's `order`, `profileBound` and `ratioBound`, and `ring` closes the goal for any slopes. `referenceSelf_constant` becomes `P.referenceFamily_constant ... t t`. There are no degenerate cases, because the constant is independent of the slopes.
findings.benefit: The statement then expresses the actual fact (restricting to a reference cone only changes the carrier bound to F*cone) for every reference family. Downstream constructions with distinct old and new slopes, such as `assignedReferenceFamily`, could cite one lemma instead of re-unfolding `referenceFamily`. The self-slope uses in SourceLabeledNarrowTail remain available as a specialisation.
